future_real_mode_consent: Future real WiFi CSI use requires explicit consent from the operator, intended subject, and all potentially affected people in the sensing area. references.purpose: ESP32 CSI collection, CSV parsing, model training, Jetson Nano inference, MQTT publishing, and Android subscriber example for human-activity sensing.
hardware_assumptions: Two ESP32 microcontrollers commonly used as AP and station for active collection.
Jetson Nano edge inference is referenced.
WiFi credentials, ESP-IDF v4.3, serial monitor, SD card, and MQTT server may be involved.
supported_capture_path: active_sta sends packet requests to an AP and receives CSI packet responses.
active_ap accepts stations and receives CSI packet responses.
passive listens on a configured channel.
idf.py flash monitor and serial output are the documented collection path.
data_formats: CSV files written from serial monitor or SD card.
Parsed CSI amplitude and phase arrays.
Notebook/model artifacts under notebooks and models.
dependencies: ESP-IDF v4.3 for firmware build/flash paths.
Python analysis utilities reference numpy, matplotlib, pandas, scikit-learn style workflows, TensorRT/CUDA, paho MQTT, and serial access.
Utilities contain HiveMQ Cloud endpoint usage and hardcoded JetsonNano MQTT credentials; these must not be reused.
No dependencies were installed for Phase 8A.
useful_method_ideas: CSV as a future sample-pack fixture format after consent and hardware review.
Separate capture metadata from model inference metadata.
Record clock synchronization and local timestamping limitations for future capture provenance.
somatic_should_not_adopt: Do not flash ESP32 firmware, open serial ports, publish MQTT messages, run TensorRT/CUDA inference, or reuse notebooks as Somatic runtime.
Do not adopt the root repository until license status is resolved.
privacy_security_cautions: Active and passive CSI collection can observe people in a physical environment, including bystanders.
Serial CSI logs, SD-card CSVs, raw RF/CSI, derived features, activity labels, MQTT messages, and Android subscriber outputs are sensitive by default.
MQTT/Android publishing and raw CSI CSV export require explicit consent, retention controls, authentication, and network review.
